message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"10.21","text":"For most people say, “In our objects of worship, we venerate not the gold, nor the silver, nor wood or stone (for we too know that these are nothing other than lifeless matter and the craftsmanship of a mortal human), but the spirit dwelling in them; this is what we call a god.” See, then, the dishonesty of those who say this. For since what is visible is easily exposed as nothing, they have fled for refuge to the invisible, as though they could not be refuted about something uncertain. Nevertheless, such people agree with us in part that one half of the cult images among them is not a god but unfeeling matter. It remains for them to show how we are to believe that it has a divine spirit. Yet they cannot demonstrate to us that it exists, since it does not—and we do not believe that they have seen it themselves. We will provide them with proofs that it does not have a divine spirit, so that lovers of truth, on hearing the refutation of this rabid supposition, may turn away from thinking that these things are animate.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"Τῶν σεβασμάτων ἡμῶν","chosen":"In our objects of worship","rationale":"σεβάσματα denotes things treated as sacred or worthy of veneration; “objects of worship” preserves the cultic sense without assuming that they are divine."},{"source_quote":"τὸ ἥμισυ τῶν παρ’ αὐτοῖς ἱδρυμάτων","chosen":"one half of the cult images among them","rationale":"ἱδρύματα refers here to erected cult objects. “One half” preserves the argument that their alleged material-and-spirit composite is already conceded to be partly mere matter."},{"source_quote":"λοιπὸν δὲ περιλείπεται δεῖξαι αὐτοῖς πῶς πιστεύομεν ὅτι· θεῖον ἔχει πνεῦμα.","chosen":"It remains for them to show how we are to believe that it has a divine spirit.","rationale":"The dative αὐτοῖς is taken as the party responsible for demonstrating the claim, while πῶς πιστεύομεν is given deliberative force in context. A more mechanically indicative rendering, “how we believe,” would conflict with the speaker’s immediately stated disbelief."},{"source_quote":"τῆς λυσσώδους ὑπονοίας","chosen":"this rabid supposition","rationale":"ὑπόνοια can mean suspicion, notion, or supposition; here it is the hostile characterization of the belief that the images are animate. λυσσώδης supplies the forceful image of rabid madness."},{"source_quote":"ἔνπνοα","chosen":"animate","rationale":"The adjective means possessing breath or life, in contrast with the objects’ lifeless material."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"10.22","text":"First, then, if you venerate them as animate, why do you also bow down before the tombs of ancient people, who admittedly did not even possess a divine spirit? Thus you are not telling the truth in this respect either. Yet if your objects of worship really were animate, they would move by themselves, would have a voice, would shake off the cobweb on them, would repel those who wish to plot against them and who steal from them, and would easily seize those stripping away the votive offerings. But now they do none of these things. Instead, like condemned prisoners—and especially the more valuable among them—they are kept under guard, as we said at the outset. Again, do not the rulers demand taxes and duties from you on their account, on the ground that you derive great profit from the things there? And have they not often been plundered by enemies and, after being smashed, divided up? Do not the priests themselves, even more than those who worship from outside, secretly remove many of the votive offerings, thereby passing judgment against themselves over their useless worship?","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἀρχαίων τάφους","chosen":"the tombs of ancient people","rationale":"The adjective modifies “tombs” across the printed punctuation, while the following genitive identifies the ancient people whose tombs are meant."},{"source_quote":"τοὺς αὐτοῖς ἐπιβουλεῦσαι θέλοντας καὶ κλέπτοντας","chosen":"those who wish to plot against them and who steal from them","rationale":"The first participle expresses hostile intent and the second actual theft. The object of κλέπτοντας is unstated; “from them” fits the surrounding discussion of images and their offerings, while “who steal them” is also possible."},{"source_quote":"οἱ τιμιώτεροι αὐτῶν","chosen":"the more valuable among them","rationale":"τίμιος can mean honored or costly. The need to guard the objects from theft makes material value the more immediate sense, though “the more honored” remains possible."},{"source_quote":"ὡς πολλὰ καρπιζομένους τῶν ἐκεῖ","chosen":"on the ground that you derive great profit from the things there","rationale":"καρπίζομαι denotes enjoying or reaping proceeds. τῶν ἐκεῖ is elliptical, referring to the things or resources located at the cult sites."},{"source_quote":"τῶν ἔξω θρησκευόντων","chosen":"those who worship from outside","rationale":"The phrase distinguishes the priests from worshipers outside the priestly group; “lay worshipers” is a contextual alternative but is more interpretive."},{"source_quote":"ἐπὶ τῇ ἀχρήστῳ θρησκείᾳ ἑαυτῶν κατεγνωκότες","chosen":"thereby passing judgment against themselves over their useless worship","rationale":"καταγιγνώσκω with the reflexive means to condemn or pass adverse judgment on oneself; the priests’ theft is presented as exposing their own worship as useless."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"τί καὶ ἀνθρώπων; ἀρχαίων τάφους προσκυνεῖτε","issue":"The printed Greek question mark separates ἀνθρώπων from ἀρχαίων τάφους, although the surviving words form the coherent phrase “tombs of ancient people” when read continuously. This appears to be an editorial-punctuation irregularity, not missing wording.","proposed_reading":"τί καὶ ἀνθρώπων ἀρχαίων τάφους προσκυνεῖτε;","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"τῶν ἐκεῖ;.","issue":"The selected edition prints both a Greek question mark and a period at the end of the question. The duplication does not affect the recoverable syntax or wording.","proposed_reading":"τῶν ἐκεῖ;","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"10.23","text":"“Yes,” he says, “but they were detected through the gods’ providence.” This is false. For how many of them have gone undetected? If, because some have been caught, they say that those gods possess power, they are mistaken. Some tomb robbers too are discovered, while others escape notice, and surely those who are caught were not detected by the power of the dead. We should understand something similar about the gods that are stolen and despoiled. “But,” he says, “the gods within them have no concern for their own carved images.” Why, then, do you yourselves tend them—scrubbing, washing, and cleaning them, crowning them, and offering sacrifices to them? Therefore recognize from this that you are not acting with sound reasoning either. For just as you weep over the dead, so you also offer sacrifices and pour libations to your gods.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ναί φησιν, ἀλλὰ προνοίᾳ αὐτῶν ἐφωράθησαν.","chosen":"“Yes,” he says, “but they were detected through the gods’ providence.”","rationale":"The first plural referent is the thieves, while αὐτῶν refers contextually to the gods or cult images credited with providential action. The nouns are made explicit in English to prevent the two pronouns from being confused."},{"source_quote":"δύναμιν αὐτοὺς ἔχειν","chosen":"that those gods possess power","rationale":"The accusative αὐτούς resumes the gods credited with detecting thieves, not the thieves who were caught."},{"source_quote":"τοὺς κλεπτομένους καὶ συλωμένους θεοὺς","chosen":"the gods that are stolen and despoiled","rationale":"Both passive participles modify the gods themselves, continuing the argument that the cult objects can be carried off and stripped."},{"source_quote":"τῶν ξοάνων αὐτῶν","chosen":"their own carved images","rationale":"ξόανον originally denotes a carved, especially wooden, cult image and can more broadly denote an idol or statue. “Carved images” preserves that material sense without requiring that every object be wooden."},{"source_quote":"τημελεῖτε σμήχοντες καὶ πλύνοντες καὶ καθαίροντες, στεφανοῦντες, ἐπιθύοντες","chosen":"tend them—scrubbing, washing, and cleaning them, crowning them, and offering sacrifices to them","rationale":"The sequence lists the physical and ritual care supplied by the worshipers. ἐπιθύω here means to offer sacrifice, not merely to desire."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"10.24","text":"Yet calling them administrators no longer accords even with the analogy of Caesar and the authorities under him, when you yourselves take all care of them, as I said before, tending your cult images in every respect. For, capable of nothing, they do nothing. So tell us: what do they administer? What do they do comparable to what the rulers in each locality do? What do they accomplish comparable to God’s stars? Unless perhaps they shine like the sun—the very ones for whom you yourselves light lamps? Can they, just as the clouds bring rains, also bring downpours—they who cannot even move themselves unless people take hold of them? Or do they provide fruits in the same way as the earth—they for whom you supply sacrifices? Thus they can do nothing.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"διοικητὰς αὐτοὺς λέγειν","chosen":"calling them administrators","rationale":"διοικητής denotes one who manages, governs, or administers. “Administrators” maintains the comparison with Caesar’s subordinate authorities."},{"source_quote":"τὰ ἱδρύματα","chosen":"cult images","rationale":"The erected objects are the material images being tended, illuminated, and physically moved; “cult images” conveys this setting better than the broader “institutions” or “establishments.”"},{"source_quote":"οἱ κατὰ τόπον ἡγούμενοι","chosen":"the rulers in each locality","rationale":"The phrase denotes leaders or governors assigned to particular places, continuing the administrative analogy."},{"source_quote":"εἰ μήτι φαίνουσιν ὡς ὁ ἥλιος, οἷς λύχνους ὑμεῖς ἅπτετε;","chosen":"Unless perhaps they shine like the sun—the very ones for whom you yourselves light lamps?","rationale":"εἰ μήτι introduces an ironic possible exception. The emphatic ὑμεῖς sharpens the contrast between supposedly shining gods and worshipers who must provide their light."},{"source_quote":"ἐὰν μὴ ἄνθρωποι ἐπιλάβωνται","chosen":"unless people take hold of them","rationale":"The middle verb means to grasp or take hold of something; here people must handle the immobile images before they can move."},{"source_quote":"τὸν αὐτὸν τῇ γῇ τρόπον","chosen":"in the same way as the earth","rationale":"The dative τῇ γῇ marks the earth as the standard of comparison for providing fruit."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"10.25","text":"And even if they were able to do something, you would not rightly call them gods, since even the elements, through which good things are supplied, may not be called gods. But only the one who ordered them to carry out everything for our use and commanded them to serve humankind—him alone do we rightly call God. Unaware of his beneficence, you proclaimed that the elements assigned to you as servants were to rule over human beings. And why is there any need to speak about the elements, when you even make lifeless statues and not only bow down before them but also think it proper to be subjected to them in every respect as servants? For this reason, you yourselves, through the things by which you lost your senses, have become subject to demons. Nevertheless, through recognition of God himself, you can by good deeds become masters again, give orders to demons as servants, and, as sons of God, be established as heirs of an eternal kingdom.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τὰ στοιχεῖα","chosen":"the elements","rationale":"The term denotes the constituent powers or elements of the natural order through which benefits are supplied; the argument denies that their usefulness makes them gods."},{"source_quote":"τὸν μόνον τάξαντα αὐτὰ πρὸς τὴν ἡμετέραν χρῆσιν ἐκτελεῖν τὰ πάντα","chosen":"only the one who ordered them to carry out everything for our use","rationale":"τάσσω expresses appointing or ordering the elements to perform their assigned functions for human use."},{"source_quote":"κελεύσαντα ἀνθρώπῳ ὑπηρετεῖν","chosen":"commanded them to serve humankind","rationale":"The singular ἀνθρώπῳ is generic, referring to humanity rather than one particular man."},{"source_quote":"τὰ ὑμῖν δοῦλα ἀπονεμηθέντα στοιχεῖα καθ’ αὐτῶν δεσπόζειν","chosen":"that the elements assigned to you as servants were to rule over human beings","rationale":"The main rendering takes αὐτῶν as a notional plural resumption of the preceding generic ἀνθρώπῳ, “humankind.” Taking it as referring to the elements themselves or to the good things would produce a much less coherent claim."},{"source_quote":"ὡς δοῦλοι κατὰ πάντα αὐτοῖς ὑποτετάχθαι","chosen":"to be subjected to them in every respect as servants","rationale":"δοῦλοι marks complete subordinate status. “Servants” follows the supplied wording policy, while “slaves” would more explicitly foreground ownership and coercive subjection."},{"source_quote":"διὰ τοῦτο ἑαυτοὺς δι’ ὧν παρεφρονήσατε, δαίμοσιν ὑποχείριοι γεγόνατε","chosen":"For this reason, you yourselves, through the things by which you lost your senses, have become subject to demons.","rationale":"The accusative ἑαυτούς is treated as a pendent emphatic expression resumed by the second-person verb. δι’ ὧν refers to the cult objects as the means or occasion of their loss of reason."},{"source_quote":"διὰ τῆς εἰς αὐτὸν τὸν θεὸν ἐπιγνώσεως ἐκ τῶν καλῶν πράξεων","chosen":"through recognition of God himself, you can by good deeds","rationale":"The main rendering attaches ἐκ τῶν καλῶν πράξεων to becoming masters again, while διὰ τῆς ... ἐπιγνώσεως gives the broader means. It could alternatively describe recognition of God as arising from good deeds."},{"source_quote":"δαίμοσιν ὡς δούλοις ἐπιτάξαι","chosen":"give orders to demons as servants","rationale":"The dative phrase identifies the demons as the servants being commanded, reversing the preceding subjection to them."},{"source_quote":"ὡς υἱοὶ θεοῦ αἰωνίου βασιλείας κληρονόμοι καταστῆναι","chosen":"as sons of God, be established as heirs of an eternal kingdom","rationale":"The main rendering attaches αἰωνίου to βασιλείας. Grammatically it could instead modify θεοῦ, yielding “as sons of the eternal God, be established as heirs of a kingdom,” but the chosen attachment gives the more natural division of the two genitive phrases."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"τὰ ὑμῖν δοῦλα ἀπονεμηθέντα στοιχεῖα καθ’ αὐτῶν δεσπόζειν ἀνηγορεύσατε","issue":"The plural αὐτῶν has no nearby plural human antecedent; its nearest explicit plural antecedents are the elements or the good things, neither of which gives the expected contrast. The translation defensibly treats it as a notional resumption of generic ἀνθρώπῳ, but καθ’ ὑμῶν, “over you,” is a plausible conjecture and is not the supplied reading.","proposed_reading":"τὰ ὑμῖν δοῦλα ἀπονεμηθέντα στοιχεῖα καθ’ ὑμῶν δεσπόζειν ἀνηγορεύσατε","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"διὰ τοῦτο ἑαυτοὺς δι’ ὧν παρεφρονήσατε, δαίμοσιν ὑποχείριοι γεγόνατε.","issue":"The accusative ἑαυτούς does not formally agree with the nominative predicate ὑποχείριοι and the second-person subject of γεγόνατε. It can be read as a pendent accusative emphasizing the people addressed, which supports the main rendering; nominative αὐτοί would be a possible conjectural regularization.","proposed_reading":"διὰ τοῦτο αὐτοὶ δι’ ὧν παρεφρονήσατε, δαίμοσιν ὑποχείριοι γεγόνατε.","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
